type: area

## Facts

- [stated] Chaired by Edgar Cortright (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)
- [stated] Traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2 (src: Apollo 13 Review Board report, 2026-10-24)
- [stated] Recommended redesigning the oxygen tank and removing electrical equipment from inside it (src: Apollo 13 Review Board report, 2026-10-24)

- [stated] Published in June 1970 (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)

name: "Oxygen tank No. 2"
type: topic
description: Apollo 13 service module tank whose 28-volt thermostatic switches failed under 65-volt power and caused the explosion
created: 2026-10-24
updated: 2026-10-24
aliases: ["oxygen tank No. 2", "O2 tank 2", "oxygen tank 2"]
---

## Facts

- [stated] Exploded on 1970-04-13, about 56 hours into the flight (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)
- [stated] Its thermostatic switches were built to a 1962 specification for 28 volts DC (src: Moonport SP-4204, 2026-10-24)
- [stated] The heater specification was revised in 1965 to 65 volts but the switches were not changed (src: Moonport SP-4204, 2026-10-24)
- [stated] Before launch it was emptied by running its heaters on 65-volt ground power for about eight hours (src: Moonport SP-4204, 2026-10-24)

content.text:
ANSWER: The Apollo 13 Review Board was chaired by Edgar Cortright, who was director of NASA Langley Research Center at the time (1970). The board traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2. Its thermostatic switches were built to a 1962 specification for 28 volts DC, but the heater specification was revised in 1965 to 65 volts and the switches were not changed. The board called the switch failure a serious oversight that all parties share.
